marks.gloss_en: if where each has a financial association and each might own all of it Sumchos divides without an oath, then where neither has any association -- and it may belong to both -- all the more so
the purchase case survives 'see who paid' only where the seller took money from both, one willingly and one under protest, and we do not know which
Ben Nanas: no oath is imposed where one of the parties is certainly swearing falsely
(entertained) the mishna cannot be Ben Nanas
the mishna can be Ben Nanas: here both may be swearing truthfully, having lifted it together
Sumchos: property of uncertain ownership is divided without an oath
the Rabbis: in property of uncertain ownership, the burden of proof rests on the claimant
for the Rabbis the mishna is fine: 'burden of proof' was said where neither grasps the property; here both grasp it, so they divide under oath
defense (a): Sumchos said his rule only for uncertain-vs-uncertain claims, not certain-vs-certain
Rabba bar Rav Huna's tradition: Sumchos said it even for certain-vs-certain claims
defense (b): Sumchos said his rule only where each litigant has an independent financial association with the item
